short: The most-produced tank in history, still being pulled out of storage to fight.
full:
Accepted for service on 8 May 1958, the T-55 was a substantially reworked T-54B: it added protection against nuclear fallout, carried more ammunition, dropped the bow machine gun and used a more powerful engine. It kept the 100 mm D-10T gun and the very low, rounded turret that made Soviet tanks hard to hit and cramped to work in. Soviet production ran to 1981, with licence manufacture in Poland and Czechoslovakia; T-54 and T-55 output together is usually put between 80,000 and 100,000 vehicles.

Exported to around fifty countries, it became the standard tank of the non-aligned and Warsaw Pact worlds and fought in Vietnam, the Middle East in 1967 and 1973, Angola, Afghanistan and Iraq. Its cheapness and simplicity have kept it alive well past obsolescence: Russia withdrew T-55s from long-term storage and returned them to the front in Ukraine from 2023, sixty-five years after they were accepted.
